findings.location: ## Definition, opening setup: the spin-structure and gauge-bundle clauses, including the sentence beginning “Let P→M be a smooth principal right G-bundle” and the construction E_R=P×_R V_R.
findings.evidence: The Definition uses Spin(d), a smooth principal right G-bundle with connection, a unitary representation, and an associated complex bundle with induced metric and connection without giving their exact mathematical definitions or citing them as dependencies. The item’s deps contain only def-aqft-thooft-anomaly. It also does not require R to be smooth, which is needed for the stated induced connection. Add exact mathematical suppliers and state their relevant right-action, quotient, smoothness, and induced-connection content.

findings.location: ## Definition, paragraph immediately after the displayed chiral Dirac map: “Assume the operator is Fredholm.”
findings.evidence: The item does not define Fredholm or list an exact dependency supplying it. Its proof then uses finite-dimensional kernels and cokernels to construct a one-dimensional determinant line. The published item def-fredholm-operator-cokernel-and-index gives the needed content: bounded map, closed range, finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel.

findings.location: ## Definition, opening paragraph: the construction of Q_Y using Spin(d+1) and the reduction to the subgroup Spin(d) fixing the first frame vector.
findings.evidence: The Definition names Spin(d+1), Spin(d), their covering maps, and the subgroup inclusion that produces the boundary spin structure, but gives no construction of these groups or the inclusion and has no exact mathematical spin-group dependency. The published item def-given-spin-and-spinc-structures-and-associated-spinor-bundles defines Spin(n) as the norm-one even subgroup of the negative-square Clifford algebra and defines its standard cover; the boundary subgroup identification still needs to be stated precisely.

findings.location: ## Definition, group declaration: “A group-like p-form global symmetry … consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group G” for all 0≤p<d.
findings.evidence: The definition allows non-Abelian G for p>0. Gaiotto, Kapustin, Seiberg, and Willett, Generalized Global Symmetries, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.5148, §1, PDF p. 3, state that the symmetry group must be Abelian for positive form degree. Add that hypothesis for p>0 or explicitly distinguish and justify a different generalized defect structure. The assigned consumer uses the p=0 SU(2) case, so this issue does not change its particular center-action calculation.

findings.location: ## Definition, paragraph beginning “Use the preceding topological-defect definition”: the inline wikilink to def-aqft-topological-defect.
findings.evidence: The complete Definition is interrupted by a hyperlink. The statement-first policy requires the Definition to remain uninterrupted and all links to move to the immediately following ## Definition references section, each on its own source line and paragraph.

findings.location: ## Definition, local anomaly class paragraph: “with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention.”
findings.evidence: The item does not define the mathematical type or set of admissible counterterms, nor specify an equivalence relation or subspace compatible with s and d_H. An arbitrary model-specific collection is not automatically the denominator of a relative cohomology group. Define the admissible counterterm space and boundary equivalence, or state the precise quotient construction. The assigned consumer uses this supplier only for the infinitesimal/global scope distinction, not for a vanishing-class inference.
